sources.title: U.S. Soccer — U11–U12 coaching guide
sources.scope: Developmental context: individual needs, fundamental technique, both-foot passing, and learning through games. This is not a solo exercise prescription.

sources.title: Coerver — Three Ways to Practice at Home
sources.scope: Supports small-space ball mastery and less-preferred-foot practice for ages 8–12. Does not validate our session lengths or level thresholds.

sources.title: The FA — 7 ways to master the ball
sources.scope: Identifies ball mastery, aerial control and staying on the ball as objectives. Group-session video is not verified here; not a mechanics reference.

sources.title: The FA / Graeme Carrick — Sole of the foot
sources.scope: Sole use can stop, roll, turn and prepare the next action. Published age band is 12–16; younger adaptations require review.

sources.title: NorCal Premier PDP — Home Skills Program
sources.scope: Individual home program includes juggling, dribbling and target/wall passing with personal tracking. Its selected-player benchmarks are not universal youth standards. Standing-on-ball activities are excluded.

sources.title: Global Futbol Training — Wall passing and first touch
sources.scope: Supports one-/two-touch wall practice, both feet and receiving with one foot then passing with the other. Our doses and progression are original proposals.

sources.title: My Personal Football Coach — Touch & Cruyff Turn
sources.scope: Describes deception, a forward touch, turn and exit; recommends both feet. Detailed contact animation still requires video review.

sources.title: SoccerDrive / Bobby Burling — Dribbling Skills Series
sources.scope: Explicitly supports solo inside/outside contacts, lateral and forward/back rolls, and freestyle combinations.

sources.title: SoccerDrive / Bobby Burling — Inside and Outside Touches
sources.scope: One-player activity uses inside/outside contacts and practices each foot; controlled repetition precedes speed.

sources.title: SoccerDrive / Bobby Burling — Trap, Roll, and Play
sources.scope: Source has TWO players: sole receive, lateral roll, opposite-foot pass. Replacing the server with a wall is our explicit adaptation.

sources.title: SoccerDrive / Bobby Burling — Turning Skills Series
sources.scope: One-player turns include pull-back and outside-foot chop. Named-turn descriptions are brief; do not infer a complete animation from the title.

sources.title: The FA / James Riches — Let’s make receiving more chaotic
sources.scope: Scanning needs useful information and receiving should connect to subsequent action. Solo predetermined routines are not equivalent to opponent-driven decisions.

sources.title: FIFA / Mauricio Marques — Ball manipulation and control
sources.scope: Individual sections emphasize control, direction and pace changes, and awareness of surroundings. Group and opposed sections are excluded from home prescriptions.

sources.title: Global Futbol Training — 3 secrets to a harder shot
sources.scope: Laces-striking discussion supports controlled approach and stable ankle contact. The article itself qualifies landing mechanics; no universal airborne/landing rule is adopted. Maximal-power training is excluded.
